messages:
Maya: quick heads-up — I posted an RFC draft for a hybrid sideload + shared-layer rollout approach for onprem/airgapped installs. looking for early feedback on tradeoffs before i turn it into a follow-up RFC.

Kevin: skimmed. big +1 for shared layers to cut bandwidth, but we need to nail activation windows and component contraction semantics. how do we avoid partial-activate for dependent components?

Maya: intention is staged activation with a small contraction window. operator chooses a window size; runtime enforces atomic activation per-component-group. if a dependent group fails, we roll back the group, not the whole node.

Lena: concern: on fully offline fleets, network-less rollback is tricky. if we rely on a seed to provide blobs, operator can run out of seeds. what guarantees do we provide for idempotent reapply?

Sam: we should distinguish two flows: seedful (seed transfer available) and seedless (single-image, shared-layers). seedless needs deterministic idempotent apply + tombstones for deleted layers. also need a compact resume token so an operator can resume without re-syncing everything.

Meera: admin UX: can we expose a dry-run mode that shows which groups will contract/expand and gives a per-node risk score? ops teams will ask for that before flipping canaries.

Maya: yes, dry-run planned. risk score = missing-seed-count + activation-window-overlap + manifest-compat-failures. UI exposes per-group diffs.

Kevin: signing model: we need both manifest-level signatures and per-layer checksums. on airgapped installs, verifying signatures requires local trust anchors — tie that into KMS/HSM if present. failure modes must be explicit: "signature-mismatch" vs "missing-anchor" vs "corrupt-chunk".

Lena: +1 on explicit failure reasons. also suggest a small, signed "activation-intent" blob that operators can store — helps offline audit and rollback reasoning.

Sam: operational note: for shared layers, dedupe policy must be pluggable. some customers will want global-dedup (single copy across nodes) vs per-node hardlinks. have a config flag and clear disk-accounting metrics.

Meera: what about staged rollout canaries? idea: pin a small cohort of nodes that opt into early activate and run health-check hooks, then expand. hooks must support async KV-cache priming for large models.

Maya: exactly. rollouts: canary -> cohort -> fleet. each step waits for health-check pass ratio and bounded activation latency. if KV priming lags, we can auto-fallback to a compatible q4/quantized variant.

Kevin: fallback compatibility mapping needs to be in the catalog manifest. also need a clear downgrade path that doesn't require seeds from old version if blobs were garbage-collected. define GC retention windows per-release.

Lena: GC retention + tombstone policy is critical. retention must be configurable per-catalog and expose a retention/test-mode in console.

Sam: small nit: add a "resume token" format example in the RFC, e.g. `resume:v1:<node-id>:<manifest-hash>:<offset>` so it's explicit how resume/replay works for partial fetches.

Maya: will add the token example and explicit failure states. also adding a short operator playbook for "seed exhaustion" and "partial-activation rollback".

deploy-bot: runbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/hybrid-sideload-rollout (draft) :memo:

Meera: next steps — Maya, can you update draft with: resume token, activation-intent blob spec, GC retention knobs, and dry-run UX? I'll pair on the operator playbook. then we can schedule an RFC follow-up in architecture sync.

Maya: yep — i'll update today and ping for a quick review. thanks all. :thumbsup:
